static_traits.name: Liu Na
static_traits.social_status: Distant relationships with peers, difficulty establishing intimate relationships; has a few friends to confide in, but their understanding of the distress is limited
static_traits.medical_history: no significant physical illness; no prior similar psychological problems; never received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: clear expression, able to describe experiences concretely; initial attitude fairly skeptical; often uses absolute and negating expressions (like 'the worst' 'never succeeding'); average cooperativeness, can try but confidence insufficient

basic_info.main_problem: I almost always feel I am the worst Graduate student, leading to Persistent self-doubt and incompetence.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent self-doubt and negative self-cognition have begun affecting academic performance and mental health, hoping to improve through counseling.

core_beliefs: I am not like my peers

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: if grades do not meet Anticipation, it means I am not suited to this field and will not succeed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: avoiding continued Learning or starting assignments, falling into Self-deprecation and Withdrawal
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I can never succeed in this field, I should drop out now

special_situations.event: Seeing classmates more confident and skilled in class or during challenging academic periods
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: if others look more confident or knowledgeable, it proves I am not capable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Frequently comparing with others, reducing deep communication with classmates
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: they all know what they are doing while I am busy with nothing, I am the worst Graduate student

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Must be perfect the first time, or it is failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will mess it up, starting is useless too

special_situations.event: Receiving good grades or professors' positive feedback
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: positive results are just luck, of no reference value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: negating positive evidence, maintaining Self-doubt and negative self-evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: this is just luck, not representing my ability

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized as competent, to have one's value and ability seen
core_conflict.fear: fear of being proven incompetent, negated by peers or mentors
defense_goal: reducing the risk of judgment and failure through self-criticism, negating positive feedback and avoiding difficult tasks

object_relations.object_representation: Critical judges or more excellent peers/mentors

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites him to focus on positive evidence or suggests questioning negative beliefs
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: believing these are self-deception or untrue, positive feedback merely luck, the counselor not understanding her real inadequacies
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: emphasizing 'this is just luck/fluke' in a calm but firm tone, listing counterexamples to weaken positive evidence, while expressing 'can try but I have no expectations'.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When facing starting a difficult academic task or being asked to try a new method
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: treating tasks as tests that can only be success or total failure, if not perfect proving oneself incompetent
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: using absolute expressions (like 'either succeed or fail'), postponing or avoiding action, refusing step-by-step attempts.

manifestations: Living alone; struggling to build close relationships with peers; frequent Self-doubt and comparison with others before/after classes and during assignments, subjectively feeling alienated from the group

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: evaluating oneself by the standard of 'must excel/cannot fail'
self-blame and negation once standards are not met

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: repeatedly reviewing inadequacies before starting tasks and thus avoiding
Dismisses positive feedback as 'luck' when receiving it

exception_events.target_problem: when facing challenging academic tasks or receiving grades below Anticipation, the client usually Catastrophizes, generating strong Anxiety and avoiding starting or continuing assignments, leading to declining performance.
exception_events.unique_outcome: in some coursework or exams, the client achieved good grades and received positive comments from professors; was able to complete tasks and Gain recognition then, showing a better outcome than usual.
exception_events.reason: clues: different context (tasks better matched ability); different approach (more focused or completing tasks as planned); different support (professor's clear positive feedback added visible achievement evidence).

positive_force: Has obtained good grades and positive feedback from professors; there is objective evidence of competence
Willing to try counseling and reality testing, with willingness to change
Has a few friends to confide in; has some social support
Has tried positive self-talk and mindfulness practice, with self-help awareness
negative_force: Persistent comparison with others and dependence on external recognition
catastrophizing and all-or-nothing thinking Reinforcing the negative self-concept
task-starting avoidance and procrastination, temporarily easing Anxiety but harming performance
attributing positive evidence to luck, negating positive experiences
Sleep and diet affected, lowering energy and focus

target_behavior.behavior: task-starting avoidance and procrastination on academic tasks (with strong Anxiety and Self-denial)
antecedent: When reviewing notes before or after class
target_behavior.core_reason: catastrophic cognitions about failure and all-or-nothing standards, plus comparison-triggered inferiority and incompetence
target_behavior.function: escaping anticipated failure and negative evaluation, temporarily reducing Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Declining academic performance, struggling to build relationships with peers,Sleep and eating habits affected,Persistent self-doubt
